IX. ANY IRREVERSIBLE AND IRRETRIEVABLE COMMITMENTS OF RESOURCES WHICH WOULD BE INVOLVED IN THE PROPOSED ACTION
Resources that will be irretrievable after the project has been completed are materials to repair the streets and sidewalks, paving material for the parking areas and the energy to power project area lighting. The property rehabilitation program will consume the largest amount of material. Although, the actual rehabilitation of individual properties is not a project undertaking, it will result from actions related to the project. Copper, steel, lumber, plastics, aluminum, and petroleum are some of the major items to be used in the rehabilitation program. A number of existing dwelling units, and the resources of which they were constructed, will be lost to demolition activities. The loss in dwelling units will be eventually offset by the reestablishment of units in the project and elsewhere in the general area. To offset this the Redevelopment Authority will also comply with Section 105(f) of the Housing Act of 1949, as amended pertaining to low and moderate income housing, which states the newly constructed residential areas shall provide a range and distribution of housing choices so that the net aggregate of the community's approved predominantly residential urban renewal projects provides at least 51% of all housing units constructed therin be for low-moderate income families and individuals, and no less than 20% be for low income families and individuals.
